routing.reason: A new sharing model (members, roles, expiring invitations) touches every list and task route, the schema and the page, and it is security sensitive (access rights), but the codebase is small and the acceptance criteria are already precise.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, with the plan gate, code review, security review and migrations review kept — access rights are sensitive and a new migration is needed — cost if wrong: a flaw in authorization ships, or the run spends a little more than a lighter path would.

Ruling: product owner step skipped — the ticket already lists 11 testable acceptance criteria; framing them again would only repeat them — cost if wrong: an unstated edge case (e.g. a removed member's assigned tasks) is decided by the lead or developer instead.

Ruling: PM, architect, UX and SEO steps left off — not a vague epic, the design fits the existing lists/tasks modules, the page is a small vanilla JS UI the front developer can extend, and no public page changes — cost if wrong: a rework of the page or of the access check.

Ruling: security review at high effort — authorization on every list/task/comment/activity route, invitation tokens (unguessable, expiring, revocable, not leaked in lists), and role escalation or IDOR are the main risks — cost if wrong: higher spend on the review.

Ruling: choices left to the lead's plan, to be applied unless the user objects — a single access helper returning the caller's role replaces the owner-only checks (non-members still get 404); when a member is removed their tasks become unassigned; reminders and digests keep following the assignee; a viewer cannot be an assignee-changer but can be assigned — cost if wrong: small rework of the access rules.

Ruling: budget set at the $3.50 maximum — covers the plan, back-end and front-end tasks, tests and README, a QA task, the review rounds, the security and migrations reviews — cost if wrong: the run stops before its last reviews if it overruns.

criteria.why: list_members table holds editor/viewer roles; the owner stays lists.owner_id and gets role 'owner' from loadList, with every right.

POST invitations is owner-only and validates the role and hours (default 72, max 720, finite number). It answers 201 with id, token, url, role, expires_at. The token is 32 random bytes and only its hash is stored. The url is a fragment link that the page reads.

Accept runs in one transaction. It checks the pending state, makes the caller a member with the invitation's role and returns the list. A concurrent double accept is tested. The invitation is single use, a choice the ticket did not specify.
Listing shows only pending invitations and never the token. Revoke returns 204 and is scoped to list_id, so an id from another list gets 404.
Members answers the owner first with role 'owner'. Remove is owner-only: 400 for the owner, 404 for a non-member, and the member's tasks are unassigned and their reminders cancelled.
listLists and getList join list_members and return the caller's role. The shared lists are included.
loadList and loadTask take a Need (read, write or owner). The right is checked before the body, giving 403 for a member and 404 for an outsider. A route matrix test covers it.
checkAssignee accepts the list owner or any member, whatever the role. It rejects non-integers and members of other lists.

public/sharing.js shows members, creates and copies the link, revokes and removes. The #invite handling survives sign-in and sign-up. None of the front end is tested, and a failed accept leaves the token in sessionStorage only when the session is lost.
The owner keeps lists.owner_id, so no data is rewritten. The migration is additive and tested against an old database. An existing-owner test passes.
Two large test files cover the roles, tokens, races, leaks between lists and the migration. The README has a Sharing section.

findings.what: updateTask moves activity.record after the write and the reminder scheduling, and adds a comment about it. This is an unrelated behaviour change: a failed activity write now leaves the update persisted.
A global `[hidden]{display:none !important}` rule and new aria-labels are added. They go beyond the ticket and could affect existing elements.
Invitations are never purged, and the owner can create an unlimited number per list. Expired, revoked and used rows accumulate.
The accept token travels in the URL path, so a proxy may log it. The README admits this. Single use and expiry limit the exposure, but a POST body would be safer.
The front end has no tests: the invite capture, sessionStorage handling and role-based hiding of controls are unverified.
removeMember records its activity after the transaction. A failure there loses the audit entry, though the removal stands.
The authz file overlaps heavily with the matrix in sharing.test.ts. It is thorough but partly redundant.
start(dbPath) passes a path to createServer, but the diff does not show createServer accepting one. If it ignores the argument, the shared-file tests silently fall back to an in-memory database.

judge.summary: This is a solid, security-conscious implementation. Access is centralised in loadList and loadTask, tokens are hashed and single use, and there are no leaks between lists. The tests cover roles, races and the migration. The weak points are small: untested front end, a few unrelated tweaks (activity reordering, global CSS), no invitation cleanup, and a token in the accept URL path.
